CausalChain: Activated CAFs -> Secretion of exosomes loaded with specific miRNAs -> Uptake of exosomal miRNAs by tumor cells -> miRNAs target negative regulators of IL-6 receptor/modulate its variants -> Upregulation/sensitization of IL-6 signaling in tumor cells -> Enhanced activation of JAK2/STAT3 pathway -> Induction of EMT and chemoresistance -> Increased metastatic potential
Hypothesis: Exosomal miRNAs secreted by activated CAFs not only reinforce, but also prime tumor cells for heightened IL-6 responsiveness by targeting negative regulators of the IL-6 receptor and modulating its isoforms. This modulation leads to an amplified IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling cascade that drives EMT, chemoresistance, and metastasis. The integration of advanced omics technologies and AI-driven analyses will facilitate the identification of these key miRNAs. Furthermore, a combinatorial therapeutic approach that inhibits both exosomal miRNA packaging/release and the IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathway is expected to synergistically suppress tumor progression and effectively counteract chemoresistance.
Abstract: We propose that cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs), once activated in the tumor microenvironment, release exosomes enriched with specific microRNAs (miRNAs) that do more than merely reinforce IL‐6-induced JAK2/STAT3 signaling in tumor cells. Rather, these exosomal miRNAs target key negative regulators of IL-6 receptor expression and modulate receptor splicing variants, thereby priming tumor cells for an amplified response to IL‐6. This priming results in a potentiation of the canonical IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 pathway which further drives epithelial‐to‐mesenchymal transition (EMT), chemoresistance, and metastatic behavior. Leveraging contemporary omics techniques—such as single-cell RNA sequencing, high-throughput miRNA profiling, and AI-driven drug screening—we aim to identify these critical miRNA species and validate their mechanistic roles. The novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy envisaged involves concurrently targeting exosomal miRNA packaging/release (using engineered exosome interference molecules) and IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 signal transduction. This dual intervention is hypothesized to synergistically impede tumor progression and overcome drug resistance.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis posited that CAF-derived exosomal miRNAs reinforce IL-6-induced JAK2/STAT3 signaling via a feed-forward loop that promotes EMT, chemoresistance, and metastasis, suggesting a combinatorial inhibition strategy. The revised hypothesis retains the original causal chain but enhances specificity and novelty by: 1) Identifying the role of exosomal miRNAs in targeting negative regulators of IL-6 receptor expression and modulating receptor isoforms, thereby priming tumor cells for a heightened IL-6 response; 2) Integrating contemporary omics techniques and AI-driven drug discovery to identify and validate candidate miRNAs; and 3) Proposing a more detailed combinatorial intervention that targets both the exosomal miRNA release mechanism and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling. This refined approach provides greater mechanistic insight and practical translational potential.
